bullets.title: S&P 500 hits new all-time high; Mag 7 posts strongest 3-day gain since May 2025
bullets.body: The S&P 500 broke to a fresh intraday record high, roughly 4% off the prior Wednesday lows, with the Nasdaq 100 up 9% over the same stretch and nearly exiting correction territory. The Magnificent Seven led the charge with their strongest three-day gain since May 2025; Bespoke notes 70% of S&P 500 names are now above their 200-day moving averages, the highest reading in 12 months. SocGen sees S&P at 8,000, citing an 86% earnings beat rate and record-high profit margins of 16.7%.

bullets.title: Gamma squeeze + negative gamma at 6th-largest on record fueling momentum panic
bullets.body: Nomura's Charlie McElligott flagged the market is in the 6th-largest negative gamma episode on record, driven by leveraged ETF rebalancing and call buying; separately, multiple sources documented $30M+ OTM SPY call prints and sustained QQQ call flow. The setup is described as FOMO/momentum panic following July de-risking, with vol-up/spot-up dynamics (VIX rising alongside equities) confirming a gamma squeeze is in full effect.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz reopening narrative drives oil -5% and market 'blowout' today
bullets.body: Oil prices fell sharply—Brent -4.7%, WTI -5.4%—as Iran signaled willingness to allow European nations to clear Strait of Hormuz mines and Iran-Oman talks were assessed as 'positive' at technical and political levels. Treasury Secretary Bessent suggested a deal could materialize Tuesday or Wednesday, though Rubio said nothing is final and shipping analysts noted fewer than 10 ships in current traffic patterns. Iran has separately demanded transit fees, security guarantees, and sanctions relief as conditions.

bullets.title: Bessent signals dovish Fed pivot: shifts from 'cut' to 'don't hike,' Fed FIMA repo repurposed for yen defense
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent's rate stance has shifted from pushing for cuts in January to signaling 'don't hike' in August, embedding a dovish bias in ostensibly neutral language. Separately, Bessent is repurposing a Fed pandemic-era dollar backstop (FIMA repo, $60B cap) to support Japan's yen defense, despite having previously flagged Fed mission creep concerns. Philadelphia Fed President Paulson backed the July hold, said policy is 'mildly restrictive,' and warned that further action would follow if inflation progress stalls.

bullets.title: JOLTS and factory orders both miss; Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 5.86% vs. bank consensus of 2.0%
bullets.body: June JOLTS job openings came in at 7.359M, below the 7.454M consensus and down from 7.594M prior; core factory orders posted their largest unexpected plunge in a year. Durable goods beat (0.5% vs. 0.3% exp), providing a partial offset. Atlanta Fed GDPNow fell to 5.86% from 6.18%, creating a stark divergence with the average bank Q3 GDP forecast of 2.0%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q2 earnings tracking 47% YoY growth, record 16.7% profit margins; Citadel says July 'reset' the structural bull
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q2 earnings are on pace for 47% YoY growth, the highest since Q2 2021, with profit margins at a record 16.7%. Over 80% of reporting companies have beaten estimates. Citadel Securities' chief strategist argues July's selloff reset rather than ended the structural bull, with fundamentals back in focus.

bullets.title: U.S. trade deficit narrowed 5% to $73.3B in June, but remains near pre-tariff levels
bullets.body: The June trade deficit came in at $73.3B, narrowing more than 5% from May's $77.6B and down ~7.5% YTD vs. first-half 2024. Despite over a year of tariff policy, the deficit remains only slightly below pre-Trump levels. The Supreme Court invalidated most tariffs earlier this year, prompting a new round imposed under different legal authority last month.

bullets.title: AI capex demand seen strong 9-12+ months; hyperscalers under-earning as Blackwell rents at ~$2/hr
bullets.body: Multiple macro bulls see AI capex demand sustained for at least 9-12 months, with lagging cyclicals (housing, office) expected to inflect. A counterpoint from Gavin Baker: a top-tier AI startup is renting Blackwell clusters at mid-$2/GPU hour, implying compressed hyperscaler utilization economics. Hirtle's CIO separately warned the AI rally is entering a 'kindness of strangers' phase as hyperscalers shift to debt amid weakening free cash flow.

bullets.title: FCC drafting ban on Chinese optical transceivers for AI data centers; supply chain decoupling underway
bullets.body: The FCC is drafting a rule to block imports of new Chinese optical transceiver models used in AI data centers, mirroring the semiconductor supply-chain decoupling playbook. InnoLight, a key Chinese supplier, derives 57-62% of revenue from U.S. customers; the rule would benefit domestic suppliers AAOI (up 18%), LITE (up 7%), COHR, CIEN, and AXTI. A broader US supply chain restriction list now tracks 45 constraints, with fears further bans could slow buildout timelines.

bullets.title: Trump administration preparing polysilicon price floor and tariffs; solar and chip sectors affected
bullets.body: The Trump administration is preparing a price floor and new tariffs on polysilicon imports later this month, targeting derivative products used in chips and solar panels. The move aims to protect U.S. producers including Hemlock Semiconductor (owned by Corning/GLW). Combined with existing tariff actions, the policy adds further cost pressure to solar and semiconductor supply chains.

bullets.title: Tech sector forward P/E at ~20x, near year lows and below 10-year avg of 23x—valuation compression
bullets.body: Bespoke data shows the tech sector forward P/E at approximately 20x, near its lowest point of the year and below the 10-year historical average of 23x. Goldman Sachs separately notes the valuation premium for the top-five mega-cap stocks has 'almost evaporated.' Record low S&P 500 correlation historically precedes disappointing forward returns, per Owen Lamont research.

bullets.title: Semiconductors down $1.5T while S&P hits ATH; SOX/S&P divergence implies sector mispricing
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector has lost $1.5 trillion in market cap while the S&P 500 trades near all-time highs, creating one of the sharpest recent sector-vs-index divergences. Trendforce flags DRAM supply constraints through 2027, with NVDA evaluating multiple HBM4 variants for Rubin Ultra amid HBM4e validation risks. BofA reiterates MU Buy with $1,550 PT, calling the pullback an 'enhanced buying opportunity' as memory pricing normalization is expected 2027-2028.

bullets.title: Storage converging with memory: SK Hynix/SanDisk launch first High Bandwidth Flash at FMS 2026
bullets.body: SK Hynix and SanDisk released the first OCP High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) specification at Flash Memory Summit 2026, a milestone that enables GPUs to access storage in microseconds for long-context AI inference. NVDA's FMS messaging explicitly frames storage as 'beginning to behave more like memory.' Agentic AI is expected to require entirely new storage architectures, with significant AI storage announcements expected from FMS this week.

bullets.title: S&P 500 expansion reaches 74 months, above 67-month historical average; recession risk near zero at ATH
bullets.body: The current U.S. economic expansion has lasted 74 months, above the post-1949 historical average of 67 months, though well below the 128-month record. Historical data shows no U.S. recession has ever begun in a month when the S&P 500 hit a new all-time high, making inflation and rate policy the primary near-term risks rather than recession.

bullets.title: BOE rate hike expectations fully priced out; European equities modestly higher
bullets.body: Traders no longer expect a 25bp rate increase from the Bank of England this year, a notable shift from prior market pricing. European indices traded modestly higher: DAX +0.85%, CAC 40 +0.52%, FTSE 100 +0.30%, IBEX +0.38%.

bullets.title: Wage growth slowing, household dissaving funding spending; 63% of Americans paycheck-to-paycheck
bullets.body: The most comprehensive wage growth data released last week showed continued deceleration, with household spending increasingly financed by dissaving rather than income gains. Wells Fargo projects paychecks will ultimately rise faster than inflation, but 63% of Americans currently report living paycheck-to-paycheck per CNBC. U.S. wages and salaries as a share of GDP have fallen to 43%, near the lowest since records began in 1929.

bullets.title: Copper breaks $14,000 as commodity volatility extends beyond oil
bullets.body: Copper traded above $14,000/ton during the session, with commodity market attention split between oil's geopolitical-driven sell-off and copper's demand-driven strength. Codelco temporarily suspended its Andes Norte project over new seismic concerns, adding potential supply-side support for copper prices.

bullets.title: U.S. precision strike missile stockpiles 'virtually depleted' in Iran conflict; SPR on pace for historic lows
bullets.body: U.S. Central Command has redirected 45 commercial vessels as part of Iran blockade enforcement, while a report indicates ATACM inventories are at critically low levels after the Iran conflict. The Strategic Petroleum Reserve is reportedly on pace to reach its lowest level in recorded history by late September, adding structural energy security risk.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: open-weight AI models (Kimi, Qwen, Llama) expand market, don't threaten leaders
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues the rise of open-weight AI models should accelerate enterprise AI adoption by lowering costs, and are unlikely to hurt industry leaders. Separately, Anthropic has secured a $10B computing infrastructure deal and pioneered the enterprise-focused agentic AI model (token-based pricing), which OpenAI has since adopted. GIGABYTE hiked GPU prices up to 40%, with a Japanese retailer canceling pre-orders it couldn't fulfill.

bullets.title: Most-shorted stocks crushing consensus longs for 14th consecutive year amid short-squeeze dynamics
bullets.body: Per ZeroHedge/macro commentary, the most shorted stocks have outperformed consensus long picks for 14 straight years, driven by relentless short squeezes. The current episode includes PLTR (+27% on earnings short squeeze) and the broader 'negative gamma' setup that is amplifying momentum moves across the tape.
